name: Non-Hodgkin Lymphoma

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: WHO Classification of Tumours of Haematopoietic and Lymphoid Tissues

criteria.description: Histopathological confirmation of malignant lymphoid cells on lymph node or extranodal tissue biopsy
Immunophenotypic analysis demonstrating B-cell or T-cell lineage markers consistent with NHL subtype
Radiological evidence of lymphadenopathy or extranodal masses on CT, PET-CT, or MRI
Bone marrow biopsy showing infiltration by malignant lymphoid cells

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological confirmation with immunophenotyping is required; imaging and bone marrow biopsy are supportive but not mandatory.
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires integration of morphology, immunophenotyping, and clinical findings per WHO guidelines.

pathognomonic.notes: Typically firm, non-tender enlarged lymph nodes

pathognomonic.symptomName: B symptoms (fever >38°C, drenching night sweats, unexplained weight loss >10%)

common.notes: Enlarged spleen detectable on physical exam or imaging
Liver enlargement may be present in advanced disease
Common sites include gastrointestinal tract, skin, and CNS
Secondary to bone marrow involvement or chronic disease
searchTerms: fatigue related to low red blood cells

occasional.notes: May be associated with cytokine release
Due to nerve infiltration or paraneoplastic phenomena
Due to immunosuppression or marrow failure

rare.notes: Autoimmune destruction of red blood cells
searchTerms: autoimmune destruction of red blood cells

laboratory: Anemia and cytopenias on complete blood count
Abnormal peripheral blood smear in leukemic phase
imaging: CT or PET-CT showing widespread lymphadenopathy
Extranodal mass lesions on MRI or CT
Splenomegaly and hepatomegaly on ultrasound or CT
genetic: Chromosomal translocations such as t(14;18)(q32;q21) in follicular lymphoma
MYC gene rearrangements in aggressive subtypes
Clonal immunoglobulin or T-cell receptor gene rearrangements
other: Immunohistochemistry positive for CD20 (B-cell NHL) or CD3 (T-cell NHL)

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of Reed-Sternberg cells on biopsy
More predictable contiguous lymph node spread
Peripheral blood lymphocytosis with mature small lymphocytes

redFlags: Unexplained persistent fever and night sweats
Sudden onset of severe cytopenias or organ dysfunction
references: Swerdlow SH, Campo E, Harris NL, et al. WHO Classification of Tumours of Haematopoietic and Lymphoid Tissues. IARC; 2017.
National Comprehensive Cancer Network (NCCN) Guidelines for Non-Hodgkin Lymphomas, Version 6.2023.
